name: Credit spreads
summary: US high-yield spreads 3.76% on 20 Nov, a one-year high but inside the 4% Watch line
state: The US high-yield option-adjusted spread was 3.76% on 20 Nov, the latest reading, 36bp wider on the month, about 16% wider on the week and at its one-year high (FRED). The level and the monthly change remain inside the 4% and 100bp Watch lines, but spreads have widened steadily alongside the equity sell-off.
for_you: Wider spreads raise borrowing costs for lower-rated companies. Funds holding high-yield bonds are exposed if spreads keep widening.

sources.title: FRED — ICE BofA US High Yield Index OAS

why: High-yield spreads show how much lenders demand to fund weaker companies — an early warning of defaults and credit crunches.
drivers: Default expectations, risk appetite, rates, private-credit stress, fund outflows.

rubric.alert: HY OAS > 6.0%, or widened > 200bp in a month.
rubric.watch: HY OAS 4.0–6.0%, or widened > 100bp in a month.
